newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong bourse proposes moves to beef up market.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong bourse proposes moves to beef up market.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong unveiled proposals on Thursday designed to spur activity at the world's eighth largest stock market, including an expansion in trading hours and order sizes.

"It is the Exchange's mission to maintain and enhance the position of Hong Kong as an international financial centre so that it can meet the challenges of the future," the consultation paper, distributed to exchange members, said.
The proposals included the introduction of a pre-opening session and a later market close which would bring Hong Kong in head-on competition with London.
Hong Kong's current trading hours consist of a morning session from 10 a.m. (0200 GMT) to 12:30 p.m. (0430 GMT) and an afternoon session from 2:30 p.m. (0630 GMT) to 3:55 p.m. (0755 GMT).
But Hong Kong stocks can be traded in London from 4:30 p.m. (0830 GMT) in the British summer and 5:30 p.m. (0930 GMT) in winter.
"The responsibility of the Exchange is to determine whether the marginal profit, or gains, would be any larger than the marginal cost," said exchange deputy chief executive Alec Tsui.
Tsui takes over as the bourse's chief executive on February 1 when current chief Paul Chow retires.

"Initially, the pre-opening session may operate from 9:30 a.m. to 9:45 a.m. for order entry. Matching will take place between 9:45 and and 10 a.m. after which the market will be open for continuous trading," the consultation paper said.
An equilibrium price, at which most of the volume in a certain security would trade, would be calculated in the pre-opening and become the opening price for the day's trading.

The paper also proposed an extension of the closing time allowing deals to be executed either on the trading floor or on off-floor terminals, or through an evening session allowing trades exclusively through second, off-floor terminals.
"It might re-capture some of the trade supposedly lost to the London market and hence would generate more local trades," it said.
A period from 5 p.m. (0900 GMT) to 6 p.m. (1000 GMT) was suggested for an evening session, when London orders for Hong Kong stocks would be at their highest.
"The competition, of course, will mean that it is up to the investor to decide in which market to execute its order," said Tsui.

"Of course the cost of the transaction is one of the factors and another factor would be the investor's confidence in the market as well as the transparency of the market and the source of information of the investor."
Tsui said the exchange would be keen to implement longer hours quickly if members agreed and it would take two to three months to address operational issues and prepare the market.
He said Hong Kong was prepared for the competition.
In preparation for a more active market, the stock exchange proposed boosting the maximum order size and outstanding orders per broker to 400 from a current 200 for both.
The exchange also proposed enhanced access to its Automatic Order Matching and Execution System (AMS) through multiple workstations, an open gateway and order routing.

Market players have been invited to submit their views by March 21. "We hope for the time being that we will be able to have a report ready in three to four months time," said Tsui. "We hope that we will be able to follow this up rather quickly."
